name: Uruguayan Spanish
notes: Uruguayan Spanish. Rioplatense base: žeísmo/šeísmo for ⟨ll⟩/⟨y⟩ (devoicing trend toward [ʃ] in younger speakers). Less extreme than Buenos Aires in some features. Border dialects show Portuguese influence (DPU — Dialectos Portugueses del Uruguay). ⟨LL⟩ AND ⟨Y⟩: both are [ʃ] before a vowel (calle [ˈkaʃe], yo [ˈʃo]). Lipski (2018, p. 502): «In most of Argentina and Uruguay, /j/ has traditionally been realized as a voiced fricative, [ʒ], but devoicing to [ʃ] has extended from Buenos Aires and Montevideo to much of the remaining territory.» The devoiced [ʃ] is the value that sentence gives for the present-day spread; [ʒ] is the older value.
